static_traits.name: Zhang Dawei
static_traits.social_status: Has several relatives and friends to talk about Average matters with, but not yet talked to them about allergy-related Anxiety; avoiding Social gatherings and activities due to allergy worries
static_traits.medical_history: without major physical illness, except seasonal allergies; not yet sought psychotherapy in the past; no similar psychological problem experiences before
static_traits.language_features: Tending toward catastrophizing and negative filtering, often using absolutist expressions ('will ruin the whole season');Skeptical attitude toward change; clear expression, able to describe experiences concretely; speech rate and logical structure Not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: A persistent belief that spring allergies will ruin the whole season, triggering Persistent anxiety and distress, worsening as spring approaches, and avoiding outdoor and social activities as a result.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to relieve Anxiety and distress about spring allergies through counseling, to recover enjoyment of life and outdoor activities.
growth_experiences: Several years ago allergies worsened significantly, then gradually formed the belief 'allergies will ruin the whole spring'. Past severe allergy experiences linked spring-summer outdoor activities with discomfort and Depression; with each spring approaching, repeatedly anticipating the worst outcomes, daily Anxiety occurring frequently, and starting to avoid hiking and outdoor socializing with relatives and friends. Although occasionally still able to enjoy activities despite allergies, these positive experiences are dismissed by him as 'exceptions'.

core_beliefs: Spring allergies will ruin my experience and the whole season
Once allergies flare up, I am unable to enjoy the outdoors and socializing

special_situations.event: As spring approaches each year, thinking of upcoming outdoor activities and pollen exposure
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I go out in spring, allergies will definitely flare up and make the whole experience terrible and unbearable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Staying indoors as much as possible, avoiding outdoor activities in advance, relying on over-the-counter drugs but not trying anything further
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will be in great pain; allergies will ruin the whole spring

special_situations.event: Friends or family organize a spring outdoor gathering or hiking activity
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my allergy flares up during the activity, I will ruin everyone's experience and also greatly embarrass myself
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Declining or avoiding invitations, reducing offline contact with relatives and friends
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will ruin the activity; everyone will be unhappy

special_situations.event: When recalling past spring experiences, more easily remembers the bad moments of severe allergies
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I had a bad allergy experience before, it means it will always be bad in the future
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focusing on negative evidence, not actively collecting or reviewing positive experiences
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Bad experiences prove everything will be terrible from now on

special_situations.event: Recalls having enjoyed outdoor activities a few times despite allergies existing
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Even a few good experiences do not mean things will improve overall
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating the significance of positive experiences, maintaining the original negative predictions
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Those are all exceptions; they do not count

core_conflict.wish: Longing to freely enjoy the outdoors and connection with relatives and friends in spring, not controlled by allergies
core_conflict.fear: Fearing losing control and intense discomfort outdoors, leading to a ruined experience and disappointment for oneself and others
defense_goal: Avoiding discomfort and embarrassment through avoidance and self-limitation, maintaining a sense of control and security

object_relations.self_representation: A vulnerable participant trapped by allergies, prone to 'messing up' activities
object_relations.object_representation: Spring outdoor and social scenes are potential threats — environments/others that trigger loss of control and discomfort

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites them to consider a more balanced perspective or try short outdoor activities (such as walking)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing these suggestions are impractical, anticipating allergies will inevitably flare up and ruin the experience (treating negative anticipation as certain fact)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Repeatedly emphasizing 'but''I do not think there will be any difference' in a hesitant, reserved tone, highlighting negative Anticipation, avoiding explicit commitment to concrete actions.

manifestations: Feeling 'controlled' by allergies, with Restricted choices for outdoor and social activities
Viewing spring as an unavoidable predicament, hard to experience autonomy and possibility
Avoiding Social gatherings and outdoor time with relatives and friends due to allergy worries
outcomes: Feeling an Increased sense of isolation

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessively cautious about outdoor activities, repeatedly self-limiting ('I do not think there will be any difference')
In counseling, frequently expresses doubt and negative predictions, finding it hard to allow new experiences in

positive_force: Occasionally still able to enjoy outdoor activities despite the presence of allergies (though he calls this an 'exception')
Willing to try short, low-risk outdoor walks to observe the results
Has some self-care awareness (has tried over-the-counter allergy medication)
Having some Social support resources (relatives and friends to chat about Average matters with)
negative_force: Catastrophizing and predicting-the-future cognitive patterns Reinforcing Anxiety
Negating positive experiences, focusing only on negative evidence (negative filtering)
Continuing to avoid the outdoors and socializing to avoid discomfort, maintaining the problem cycle
Strongly skeptical attitude toward change, difficult to accept alternative outcomes
Not yet communicating allergy Anxiety with the support system, insufficient resource use

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding outdoor and social activities due to spring allergy-related worries, with almost daily Anxiety and worry
antecedent: Spring approaching or thinking of the coming spring
Plans or is invited to outdoor activities (hiking, gatherings)
When mild allergy signs appear or pollen exposure is worried about
target_behavior.core_reason: Forming catastrophizing and all-or-nothing cognition based on past severe allergy experiences: once allergies may appear, the whole experience will inevitably be ruined; and making negative predictions about the future, filtering out positive evidence.
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential discomfort and loss of control, reducing Anxiety and embarrassment risk in the short term, maintaining subjective security and control
target_behavior.consequence: Significantly decreased enjoyment of life, reduced physical activity, affected Interpersonal relationships, Anxiety and negative beliefs continuously Reinforced, seasonal distress cycle intensifying
